newsitem.title: FRANCE: France delays France Telecom sale due to election.
newsitem.headline: France delays France Telecom sale due to election.

text.p: France postponed the sale of a minority stake in France Telecom Tuesday because the privatisation would conflict with the parliamentary election called by President Jacques Chirac.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in a statement he had decided to delay the sale of France Telecom shares by four weeks because of the two-stage election, which will be conducted May 25 and June 1.
The first round of the election would have been the eve of the announcement of the France Telecom sale price.
Under the new timetable, private French investors will be allowed to reserve shares beginning around June 5. The international initial public offering will run from June 24 to July 1.
The ministry said the election would not affect the timetable for the private sale of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF expected later this year.

The sale of a 30 percent stake in France Telecom, estimated at between 160 billion ($27.8 billion) and 210 billion francs ($36.5 billion), could make France Telecom the company with the biggest market capitalisation in France, ahead of oil-group Elf-Aquitaine .
Arthuis said in his statement that the sale needed an important public information campaign, which would be difficult to conduct during an election campaign.
He said the decision confirmed the government's desire to conclude rapidly France Telecom's partial privatisation ahead of full liberalisation in the European telecommunications sector in 1998.
